summary:
EARTH JUKEBOX is an interactive scientific sonification platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into meaningful sound, helping people experience and understand our planet’s changing climate.

Using NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 global temperature data, the platform converts temperature anomalies into three complementary audio layers: Earth Melody (pitch), Earth Pulse (rhythm and intensity), and Earth Atmosphere (harmonic richness). Users can explore these layers through an interactive sound studio with customizable instruments, sound palettes, playback controls, and audio visualizations.

Combining scientific data, sound design, and interactive visualizations, EARTH JUKEBOX offers a new way to explore climate information beyond traditional charts and graphs. Its current implementation focuses on global temperature, with scope for future expansion to other Earth systems.

Hear the Planet. Understand Its Pulse.
details:
EARTH JUKEBOX

Hear the Planet. Understand Its Pulse.

1. Project Overview

EARTH JUKEBOX is an interactive scientific sonification platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, "The Earth Information Jukebox."

The project explores a different way of experiencing scientific information about our planet by transforming authentic NASA Earth observation data into meaningful sound.

Rather than relying exclusively on traditional representations such as graphs, maps and numerical measurements, EARTH JUKEBOX introduces sound as an additional channel for scientific exploration.

It combines data-driven audio generation, interactive scientific visualizations and customizable listening experiences to help users explore patterns and changes in Earth's systems.

Our central idea is simple:

What if people could not only see how our planet is changing, but also hear it?

2. Problem Statement

Earth observation missions and scientific instruments generate enormous quantities of information about the planet. This information helps researchers understand global temperatures, atmospheric conditions, ocean systems, forests, precipitation and other environmental phenomena.

However, scientific information is frequently communicated through numerical datasets, charts, maps and visualizations.

Although these methods are essential, interpreting complex patterns and long-term changes can be challenging for people without specialized scientific knowledge.

Furthermore, traditional visual exploration does not provide an auditory representation of the changing measurements.

We identified an opportunity to complement existing scientific visualizations with data-driven sound, making Earth science more interactive, engaging and accessible through an additional sensory experience.

3. Our Proposed Solution

EARTH JUKEBOX transforms scientific observations into sound through a process known as data sonification.

The platform takes structured scientific measurements, applies defined mappings between data characteristics and sound parameters, and generates audio that changes according to the underlying observations.

Users can explore the corresponding scientific visualizations while listening to the generated sound.

Our objective is not to replace conventional scientific visualization or claim that sonification independently reveals information absent from the original data.

Instead, we aim to provide another way to experience, interpret and explore scientific information.

4. Current Implementation: Global Temperature

Our primary scientifically integrated experience focuses on global temperature.

It uses authentic NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP) Version 4 global monthly temperature anomaly data.

Dataset characteristics:

  • Source: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies (GISS).
  • Dataset: GISTEMP v4.
  • Measurement: Global monthly temperature anomalies.
  • Unit: Degrees Celsius (°C).
  • Reference period: 1951–1980.
  • Historical coverage: January 1880 to October 2026.
  • Valid observations in the processed dataset: 1,762 monthly measurements.

The project includes a data processing pipeline that downloads, inspects, validates and standardizes the observations into a structured JSON dataset.

Missing observations are treated as unavailable measurements rather than being interpreted as zero.

We also incorporate NASA's Global Temperature Climate Spiral visualization as a visual resource for exploring the historical temperature record.

5. Three-Layer Scientific Sonification System

The core of EARTH JUKEBOX is its three-layer sonification experience.

A. Earth Melody — Temperature to Pitch

Earth Melody maps global temperature anomalies to musical pitch.

Changes in temperature anomaly produce corresponding changes in pitch, creating an evolving melodic representation of the historical temperature record.

B. Earth Pulse — Change to Rhythm and Intensity

Earth Pulse represents month-to-month temperature changes through rhythmic and intensity variations.

This layer provides an auditory representation of how the measurements change between consecutive observations.

C. Earth Atmosphere — Variability to Harmonic Richness

Earth Atmosphere uses changes in temperature variability to influence harmonic richness and timbre.

This adds another auditory dimension to the experience, allowing users to explore variability through changes in sound texture.

The three layers can be explored independently or combined to create a multidimensional auditory representation of the same scientific dataset.

These sounds are computationally generated representations of scientific measurements, not literal recordings of environmental sounds.

6. Interactive Sound Studio

EARTH JUKEBOX goes beyond generating a single audio output. It provides users with an interactive sound studio.

Its implemented audio capabilities include:

  • Five sound palettes: Scientific, Ambient, Orchestral, Electronic and Cinematic.
  • Instrument selection.
  • Individual volume controls for sound layers.
  • Master volume control and mute.
  • Reverb and delay effects.
  • Play, pause, stop and seek controls.
  • Playback speed adjustment.
  • Layer enable and disable controls.
  • Audio waveform visualization.
  • Frequency spectrum visualization.
  • Audio spectrogram.

These features allow users to customize how they experience the sonification while retaining the underlying relationship between the scientific dataset and the sound-generation process.

7. Scientific Data Processing Pipeline

Scientific credibility is a fundamental part of our implementation.

Our data pipeline follows these stages:

  1. Data Acquisition: Download the original NASA GISTEMP v4 global monthly temperature dataset.
  2. Data Inspection: Examine the CSV structure, columns, historical coverage and missing observations.
  3. Data Validation: Check the observations for invalid or infinite values and verify dataset integrity.
  4. Data Standardization: Convert the validated observations into a structured JSON format.
  5. Data Integration: Make the standardized observations available to the frontend and sonification engine.

The pipeline also records metadata, including the source, measurement units, reference period, coverage, validation results and dataset checksum.

This helps maintain traceability between the original scientific observations and the data used by the application.

8. Scientific Visualization

The platform combines auditory exploration with visual representations.

Current visualization components include:

  • Interactive climate surface visualization using HTML Canvas 2D.
  • Monthly temperature anomaly visualization.
  • Historical temperature timeline.
  • Annual and seasonal temperature charts.
  • Climate power spectrum visualization.
  • Audio waveform.
  • Frequency spectrum.
  • Audio spectrogram.
  • NASA Climate Spiral video asset and extracted preview frames.

These visual elements complement the sound experience and help users connect auditory changes with the underlying scientific information.

9. Technology Stack

Frontend

  • HTML5
  • CSS3
  • Vanilla JavaScript
  • HTML Canvas 2D

Data Processing

  • Python 3.14.7
  • Pandas
  • NumPy
  • Requests
  • Matplotlib
  • Pillow

Audio Engineering

  • Native Web Audio API
  • OscillatorNode
  • GainNode
  • AnalyserNode
  • ConvolverNode
  • DelayNode
  • DynamicsCompressorNode

Data and Scientific Resources

  • NASA GISS GISTEMP v4
  • NASA Scientific Visualization Studio Climate Spiral
  • CSV for raw observations
  • JSON for standardized processed observations
  • MP4 for the NASA visualization asset

Development and Processing Tools

  • Visual Studio Code
  • Git and GitHub
  • Python virtual environment
  • FFmpeg for video validation and frame processing

The current application is implemented using a lightweight frontend and browser-based audio generation architecture.

10. Innovation and Uniqueness

Scientific sonification is an established field. Our project does not claim to have invented it.

Our contribution is the way we bring together multiple complementary data-driven sound layers, interactive audio customization and scientific visualizations into a unified planetary exploration experience.

The three-layer system allows users to explore different characteristics of the same dataset through distinct auditory representations.

The platform also emphasizes the connection between scientific measurements and their sound transformations.

This creates an experience in which users can interact with scientific data through both visual and auditory channels rather than simply listening to a predefined musical composition.

11. Impact and Accessibility

EARTH JUKEBOX aims to make scientific exploration more engaging by introducing sound as an additional way to interact with complex Earth information.

Potential benefits include:

  • Providing an alternative way to explore scientific datasets.
  • Encouraging curiosity about climate and environmental systems.
  • Helping users experience changes in historical measurements through sound.
  • Supporting educational demonstrations of data sonification.
  • Complementing conventional scientific visualizations.
  • Creating opportunities for more accessible, multimodal scientific communication.

Sonification can provide an additional mode of exploration, although it does not automatically make scientific information accessible to every user. Effective accessibility also requires appropriate visual alternatives, controls and explanations.

12. Future Scope: Exploring Multiple Earth Phenomena

Our long-term vision is to expand EARTH JUKEBOX into a broader platform for exploring Earth's interconnected systems.

The planned expansion includes:

Ocean Currents: Exploring changes in ocean circulation and movement through appropriate oceanographic observations.

Atmospheric CO₂: Sonifying historical atmospheric carbon dioxide measurements and their changing concentrations.

Sea-Level Changes: Translating observed sea-level variations into meaningful auditory representations.

Deforestation: Exploring forest-cover loss and changes in vegetation through verified satellite and environmental datasets.

Wildfires: Representing wildfire activity and burned-area observations through data-driven sound.

Rainfall and Precipitation: Exploring changes in precipitation patterns and historical rainfall measurements.

Each additional phenomenon will require its own verified scientific dataset, suitable visualizations and scientifically meaningful sonification mappings.

These are planned extensions. The current scientifically integrated implementation is Global Temperature.

13. Conclusion

EARTH JUKEBOX explores how scientific data can become an experience rather than remaining only a collection of numbers and visual representations.

By combining authentic NASA observations, structured data processing, interactive visualizations and layered scientific sonification, we aim to create a new way for people to explore the changing story of our planet.

We believe that understanding Earth should not be limited to what we can see.

We didn't just turn NASA data into music. We created a new way to experience the changing story of our planet.

EARTH JUKEBOX — Hear the Planet. Understand Its Pulse.
